Hello fellow explorers. Let me start off by saying that I've avoided any sort of tips, advice or forums on this game since watching a gameplay video over a year ago. That being said, I wanted to start a spoiler free thread to share short stories or experiences you've had on your journey.

Only makes sense that I start off the thread with my own experience.

As I've started off, I eventually learned how to get into warp drive and chase down this mysterious entity called the Atlas. Warping to different solar systems got addicting fairly quickly - because you never know what you'll stumble on in the next system.

One of these systems had 3 planets, 1 of which was completely barren but full of massive pyres of Emeril. I spent a few hours mining and selling this element, since it was the first and relatively quickest way I could find to make some money. Naturally, that got boring and I flew over to explore the other planets.

The first one I arrived at was basically Siberia. Extreme cold matched by a forested landscape dotted with massive cliffs coming to a head in tiny, barren plateaus. It was while I was flying over the landscape that something shiny caught my eye on one of these plateaus, what had to be hundreds of feet in the air. I nailed the landing, hopped out and discovered a bunch of gravity balls. The value of them was staggering to the Emeril I had just spent hours farming. Not only that, the landscape was dotted with bunches of these things as far as I could see. As the cold started to clamp down on my health (which had drained staggeringly fast in this landscape) I gleefully returned to my ship - excited to make some real money.

I punch the thrusters only to find I'm fresh out of gas and there's no plutonium on my tiny spec of mountain within reach. In desperation I gather some other nearby elements - but nothing will work; and now I have an army of Sentinels enroute to destroy me. "Well, fuck."

Stranded on an island - watching my ship's shield deteriorate with the dull thud of sentinels eager to melt my flesh - I succumbed to my own stupidity in failing to check the fuel gauge. After dying 3 more times in the same manner, it dawns on me that it's entirely possible to get completely screwed in this game. But I'm determined to find a way out. I whip open the menu, flip over to saved checkpoints - and find that both previous saves land me in the exact same situation.

So here I am, perched on top of a mountain surrounded by cliffs - with no resources - and an extreme biting cold keeping me from walking to the nearest outpost to collect some fuel. Hopeless.

It's as I'm flipping through my inventory that it suddenly dawns on me. I hop out of my craft - and throw myself off the cliff. I engage my jetpack seconds before impact. Frantically I search the surroundings for plutonium. Nothing. Just a dark forest littered with gravity balls. I collect some resources to recharge my snowsuit - and the chase is on.

With my screen completely lit up from the blazes of lasers coming from the army behind me, I notice a cave in the distance. Maybe....just maybe I can make it.

With a sliver of health remaining, I hit the jackpot. A tiny outcropping of plutonium, only slightly bigger than the sliver of hope I had left in escaping this terrible fate. I collect the Pt - fire open the inventory, and with only seconds to spare, manage to transfer it to my ships inventory.

I die, hoping....praying to Atlas that this suddenly cruel universe wouldn't be so unruly as to clear my ships stocks as I pass out.

...

I made it. Fast forward to today and I'm a happy camper in a new system, with blue skies, lot's of plutonium and the living is easy.

As someone who's avoided all of the tips and tricks and spoilers - I'm having a hell of a good time in this new domain. This is the first time I've gone into a game with 0 expectations and 0 knowledge (other than a basic idea) - and it's been an unreal gaming experience for me.

Thanks for reading - hope to see some new posts soon!

So that the foremost of them having gained the top of all, and put themselves into order, they [Gauls] all but surprised the outworks, and mastered the watch, who were fast asleep; for neither man nor dog perceived their coming. But there were sacred geese kept near the temple of Juno, which at other times were plentifully fed, but now, by reason that corn and other provisions were grown scarce for all, were but in poor condition. The creature is by nature of quick sense, and apprehensive of the least noise, so that these, being moreover watchful through hunger, and restless, immediately discovered the coming of the Gauls, and, running up and down with their noise and cackling, they raised the whole camp, while the barbarians on the other side, perceiving themselves discovered, no longer endeavoured to conceal their attempt, but with shouting and violence advanced to the assault. The Romans, every one in haste snatching up the next weapon that came to hand, did what they could on the sudden occasion.

tl;dr:

Rome had recently been sacked by Gaul, and a few beleaguered defenders fortified themselves in a high position in the city and were waiting for military aid from a Roman army. At night, the Gauls began climbing up the fortified positions to sneak up on the Romans, who were asleep at their posts. A bunch of geese in a nearby temple heard the Gauls, freaked out, and inadvertently roused the Romans from slumber, who eventually beat back the Gallic soldiers, and in effect saving Rome.

Source:

Plutarch, John Dryden, and Arthur Hugh Clough. "Camillus." Plutarch's Lives. New York: Modern Library, 2001. 188. Print.
